ASP.NET Core endpoints should validate untrusted input, authenticate the caller, authorize each protected action, and return a status code that describes the outcome. These responsibilities work together but answer different questions.

resources.title: Building an ASP.NET Core Employee API: Architecture, Dependency Injection, and Configuration
resources.description: An ASP.NET Core API is easier to change when each part has a clear responsibility. Dependency injection (DI) connects these pieces while keeping their construction and lifetime in one place.
